We now found one way to do it. With the Property: quarkus.native.container-runtime-options=-v,/home/bfr/git/minical-multi/minical/build/:/project/build:z

Is that a preferred way or just a workaround for it?
@aguibert did you face a similar problem or do I not recall correctly?

yes I did face a similar problem where it appeared the base dir of the native image build happened up a dir from where it did before. We had doc that pointed to files similar to this:
`-H:ResourceConfigurationFiles=resources/main/resource-config.json`
but I got an error on native image build indicating the file could not be found. To fix it, I had to prepend a `../` to the path like this:
`-H:ResourceConfigurationFiles=../resources/main/resource-config.json`

I updated [the doc](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/5238/files) accordingly, but if @bframke is not seeing a "cannot find file" error, then it must be a different issue.
Something we need to fix then :)

Regarding that, the ResourceConfigurationFiles are not the Problem. Only ReflectionConfigurationFiles. Also tried your solution but does not work:

Caused by: java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException: /resources/main/reflect-config.json

This turns out to be a bug in how we handle the build of the native image when docker is used.

Essentially what happens is the following:

When a native image is being built, the working directory is a directory named "${artifactId}-${version}-native-image-source-jar" and resides inside the build directory (`build` for Gradle, `target` for Maven).
For gradle the resources are inside `build/resources/main/`, but that directory is never mounted inside the docker container that is used to build the native image (for maven they are in `target` which again is not mounted).

For non docker builds you can specify the proper path to the resources that are needed since there is no mounting going on and therefore all that is needed to find the correct path.

@cescoffier @gastaldi @maxandersen I think we need to formalize this and introduce new native configuration options for extra GraalVM reflection and resource files that we will ensure work in both docker and non-docker cases, thus removing the guess work and frustration from users.
